title: On-fault and remote observations of exceptionally long, supershear rupture in the 2025 M 7.7 Mandalay earthquake
abstract: Straight faults are considered prone to large supershear ruptures and seismic gaps to likely host future earthquakes. Both predictions may have been fulfilled in the magnitude ( M ) 7.7 Mandalay earthquake of 28 March 2025 on the Sagaing Fault. Exceptional video footage of the fault rupture, high-rate Global Navigation Satellite System, and seismological and remote sensing data reveal a supershear slip pulse that formed early and ruptured a well-identified seismic gap but propagated well beyond it, resulting in an exceptional rupture length of 510 kilometers. By contrast, the slip pulse observed in the video footage has subshear characteristics. These observations can be reconciled by a preferred conceptual interpretation invoking depth-dependent weakening properties, stress heterogeneity, and possible dynamic triggering. These properties allow for energetic ruptures that stay confined to the depth range locked in the interseismic period but are not confined to seismic gaps along strike.

title: Citron kinase activity controls alternative splicing events that drive prostate cancer growth
abstract: Prostate cancer (CaP) remains a major cause of cancer death in men, underscoring the need for mechanistically novel therapies. We previously identified the action of the mitotic kinase citron (CIT) kinase as a key driver of CaP progression and promising therapeutic target, but selective CIT inhibitors are not available. We therefore asked whether a better understanding of the action of CIT substrates, which execute CIT kinase action in CaP cells, can lead to novel approaches and/or alternative targets to indirectly interfere with CIT’s activity during CaP progression. In view of the enrichment in functions in alternative splicing among CIT substrates, we focus on the RNA splicing regulator THRAP3 as a representative substrate. Direct THRAP3 phosphorylation by CIT determined THRAP3’s RNA binding to CIT-controlled pre–messenger RNA targets. Cross-linking and immunoprecipitation sequencing identified a subset of CIT-dependent THRAP3-bound genes that were preferentially involved in cell proliferation. THRAP3 RNA binding was enriched in genes that undergo alternative splicing during CaP progression. CIT-dependent THRAP3-bound transcripts stimulated the growth of CaP cell lines, xenografts, patient-derived organoids, and patient-derived xenograft (PDX)–derived organoids, whereas CIT-independent THRAP3-bound transcripts from the same gene did not. An antisense oligo that blocks THRAP3’s recruitment to a CIT-dependent RNA binding site prevented the production of CIT- and THRAP3-dependent transcripts and inhibited the growth of cell lines and PDX-derived organoids representing different CaP stages and lineages but not of benign cells. Thus, CIT-mediated alternative splicing drives CaP progression, and its inhibition is a new therapeutic strategy in treatment-resistant CaP.

title: Mesoscale structures in signed networks
abstract: Mesoscale structures in signed networks have been studied under the limiting assumption of the validity of social balance theory, which predicts positive connections within groups and negative connections between groups. Here, we propose and apply a methodology that overcomes this limitation and is able to find and characterize also the different possible unbalanced structures in signed networks. Applying our methodology to 24 empirical networks, from social-political, financial, and biological domains, we find that unbalanced mesoscale structures are prevalent in real-world networks, including cases with substantial balance at the microscale of triangles. In particular, we find that assortativity often prevails regardless of the interaction sign and that core-periphery structures are typical in online social networks. Our findings highlight the complexity of mesoscale relational structures, the importance of using computational methods that are a priori agnostic to specific patterns, and the importance of independently evaluating micro- and mesoscale predictions of social balance theory.

title: Insights into temporal and spatial dynamics of short association fiber formation in the human fetal brain
abstract: Short association fibers (SAFs) form the local scaffold of cortical connectivity and support early functional specialization. However, their development before birth remains largely unknown. Using fetal diffusion magnetic resonance imaging from the Developing Human Connectome Project and histology from the Zagreb Collection of human brains, we present an in utero reconstruction of SAF pathways in the human brain. We tracked their volumetric and microstructural developmental trajectories in 243 fetuses spanning a critical period of connectome formation. We found that SAFs emerge before sulcal folding, initially as flat, loosely arranged pathways along the subplate–white matter interface, and later reorganize into coherent U-shaped bundles. Their maturation followed a sensorimotor-to-association gradient, paralleling cortical development. Nonlinear, bundle-specific trajectories captured multiphasic maturation, with subplate dynamics preceding increases in axonal coherence and early myelination. These findings reveal how the brain’s local wiring is established during prenatal development and provide insight into the origins of individual variability.

title: Surficial carbonates in mantle plume sources revealed by magnesium isotopes
abstract: Deep recycling of surficial carbonates into the mantle may play a critical role in shaping Earth’s long-term habitability, yet its contribution to the deep mantle carbon budget remains uncertain. Magnesium isotopes provide a promising tracer for addressing this issue, because of the uniquely light isotopic signatures of sedimentary carbonates. Here, we present high-precision magnesium isotopic compositions (δ 26 Mg) for 152 globally distributed plume-related lavas sampling diverse mantle end-members. We find that δ 26 Mg values below the bulk silicate Earth range are commonly associated with increasingly pronounced radiogenic isotopic signatures indicative of recycled crustal components. These features are best explained by the incorporation of isotopically light magnesium derived from subducted carbonate-bearing crustal materials into their mantle sources. On the basis of these observations, the lower mantle is estimated to contain up to ∼130 or ∼230–parts per million recycled carbon, potentially constituting a substantial portion of its total carbon budget.

title: Influenza A virus infection induces immune dysregulation in the placenta and fetus without vertical transmission in nonhuman primates
abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) infection during pregnancy is associated with stillbirth and preterm birth. We hypothesized that maternal IAV infection disrupts placental and fetal immune networks in ways that correlate with disease severity. Pregnant pigtail macaques were inoculated with IAV [A/California/07/2009 (H1N1)] and underwent delivery and fetal necropsy 5 days postinfection ( N = 11), with comparison to uninfected controls ( N = 16). Stillbirth occurred in 18% of infected pregnancies and in no controls. Although vertical transmission was not observed, low levels of viral RNA were detected in two placentas. Maternal infection was associated with induction of a type I interferon response in the placenta and altered innate and adaptive immune cell populations in the fetus. Maternal disease metrics (e.g., lung viral load and interferon-α) were rarely associated with placental immune perturbations but frequently linked to fetal immune cell populations (CD4 + and CD8 + T cells and monocyte subsets). Collectively, these data indicate that maternal IAV disease severity is associated with dysregulated fetal immunity.

title: SUMO2 deletion changes chromatin accessibility and enhances cytotoxic T cell activation and tumor infiltration
abstract: Cytotoxic T cells [cytotoxic lymphocytes (CTLs)] are crucial for adaptive immunity leading to prolonged survival and potential cures for cancer. Recent clinical data have shown that pharmacological inhibition modifies the tumor microenvironment (TME) and activates CTLs, although the mechanism is not well described. In this study, we found that T cell–specific knockout (KO) of the most prevalent SUMO paralog, Sumo2 / SUMO2 , in both mouse and human CD8 + T cells significantly enhanced CD8 + T cell activation without enhanced IFN-I (type I interferon)–responsive genes in vitro but increased chromatin accessibility at enhancer regions for AP-1 (activating protein 1) family members, including BATF and JunB, which are known to promote T cell activation and proliferation. Using antigen-specific OT1 and CAR (chimeric antigen receptor) T cell models, we found that Sumo2 KO CD8 + T cells had significantly higher tumor infiltration, as revealed by flow cytometry, immunofluorescence staining, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq), and conferred greater tumor growth inhibition than wild-type control T cells. snRNA-seq also revealed that Sumo2 KO in CD8 + T cells increased the expression of TRAIL (tumor necrosis factor–related apoptosis-inducing ligand) in vivo and activated the antitumor immune microenvironment, likely through cell-cell interaction involving more activated CTLs. These findings elucidate a novel mechanism by which SUMOylation controls CTL activation and tumor infiltration that activate antitumor immunity in the TME. SUMO2 KO can also be a potential strategy to enhance adoptive T cell therapies for solid tumors by enhancing their activation, tumor infiltration and ability to modulate the TME.

title: Standardizing Cell Ontology terms for cross-study integration in the female reproductive tract
abstract: The female reproductive tract is essential for fertility, pregnancy, and overall health, yet many of its cellular components remain poorly defined. Recent advances in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics have begun to reveal this complexity, but inconsistent naming of cell types and states has limited the ability to compare findings across studies. To address this challenge, an international group of reproductive biologists and ontology experts collaborated to harmonize annotations within Cell Ontology, focusing on the ovary, fallopian tube, and uterus. Standardized terms are proposed for major epithelial, stromal, and germ cell populations, supported by marker gene sets and anatomical linkages. This framework provides a shared reference that can be used to harmonize existing datasets and guide annotation of future studies, enabling consistent classification of oocytes, granulosa, theca, luteal, epithelial, stromal, and immune cells across tissues. By establishing a unified taxonomy, this work lays the foundation for integrating datasets, supporting cross-tissue comparisons, and advancing the understanding of reproductive biology, health, and disease.

title: Hydration channel engineering in Tröger’s base-POP membranes for mono/multivalent cation and anion discrimination
abstract: Sustainable recovery of critical resources from complex aqueous streams is constrained by membranes that fail to combine rapid ion transport with precise mono/multivalent discrimination. Here, we report Tröger’s base-derived porous organic polymer (POP) membranes with rigid, covalently crosslinked microporous frameworks that stabilize angstrom-scale transport channels while suppressing hydration-induced swelling. These membranes render rapid monovalent-ion transport with near-complete exclusion of multivalent cations and anions, including Mg 2+ , Al 3+ , SO 4 2− , and PO 4 3− . Experiments and simulations show that steric confinement, dehydration penalties, and electrostatic interactions cooperatively raise migration barriers for multivalent ions in confined channels. The membranes achieve comprehensive mono/multivalent discrimination across both cationic and anionic systems. In multistage electrodialysis, they enable stage-amplified lithium enrichment from high-Mg brines with stable long-term operation and downstream recovery of crystalline Li 2 CO 3 . They also facilitate high-purity NaCl enrichment from simulated seawater. Overall, this platform offers a durable and energy-efficient route to selective resource recovery from complex aqueous streams.

title: A helix-loop-helix gene orchestrates male fate in common carp
abstract: Fish show exceptional diversity in sex-determination mechanisms, making them a powerful system for studying how these pathways evolve. However, no definitive master sex-determining gene has yet been identified in Cyprinidae, a widely distributed and species-rich fish family. Here, we identified a male-specific gene in common carp encoding Pangu, a helix-loop-helix (HLH) domain peptide localized to Sertoli cells. Loss- and gain-of-function analyses demonstrate that pangu is both necessary and sufficient for male sex determination. Expression and reporter assays indicate that pangu represses cyp19a1a , a key regulator of ovarian differentiation, and disruption of cyp19a1a restores testicular development in the feminized phenotype of XY pangu mutants. These findings establish pangu as the master sex-determining gene in common carp and link an HLH domain peptide to sex differentiation.

title: Effects of probiotics on joint homeostasis and osteoarthritis: Development of microbe-gut-cartilage axis-on-a-chip
abstract: Although emerging evidence implicates gut microbiome-cartilage cross-talk in the pathogenesis of osteoarthritis (OA), the most common joint disease, studying this microbe-gut-joint axis remains challenging due to limitations of animal models and conventional in vitro systems. Here, we report a microbe-gut-cartilage axis-on-a-chip (MGCAoC) that recreates tissue-specific microenvironments with oxygen gradients and physiological fluid shear. The computer simulation–optimized chip design generates an anoxic-oxic interface for the gut module and enables perfusion of probiotic metabolites to human cartilage organoids without cross-contamination. Multiomics profiling suggested that probiotic metabolites may promote cartilage anabolism, potentially involving PI3K and MAPK pathway, and this effect was associated with up-regulated collagen type II and aggrecan expression while suppressing metalloproteinases. In inflamed cartilage organoids, these metabolites were associated with reduced proinflammatory signaling while preserving matrix integrity. The chondroprotective effects were confirmed using cartilage organoids derived from patients with OA treated with identified metabolites. This MGCAoC enables mechanistic investigation of gut-joint axis physiology and provides a versatile preclinical tool for screening probiotic-based OA therapeutics.

title: Insect-specific aldehyde synthase governs cuticle strength: a selective insecticide target
abstract: Cuticular sclerotization is crucial for insect adaptation and flight, historically thought to be dominantly driven by dopamine and its downstream products. In this study, we demonstrate that 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (DHPAA)—produced by DHPAA synthase (DHPAAS) and known in humans as a toxic dopamine metabolite—plays a central role. Cross-species RNAi, mechanical testing, and precursor quantification, consistently support this conclusion. In the migratory locust, we further reveal that DHPAA is essential for cuticular mechanical properties, whereas dopamine primarily regulates pigmentation. These findings establish a new paradigm for the chemistry of insect cuticle sclerotization. Then, we elucidate the catalytic mechanism of DHPAAS, laying the groundwork for its application in biosynthesis. Furthermore, we identify 2,5,2′,4′-tetrahydroxychalcone as a selective inhibitor of DHPAAS. Given that DHPAAS is insect-specific and absent in non-insect arthropods and vertebrates, our work points to a promising strategy for developing selective insecticides.

title: Senescent tumor cell membrane–based “time engine” nanosystem amplifies endoplasmic reticulum targeting for metastasis blockade
abstract: As an important component of biomimetic drug delivery systems, cell membrane–coated nanoparticles are widely used for subcellular delivery. However, the influence of cell membranes at different life cycles on subcellular delivery remains unexplored. Our previous study demonstrated that senescent tumor cell membrane–coated nanoparticles (SNP) displayed superior endoplasmic reticulum (ER) targeting efficiency in tumor cells. After inducing tumor cells into senescence, SNP showed greater accumulation in ER. Herein, we design a “time engine” nanosystem for amplified ER targeting: Firstly, ribociclib is encapsulated into SNP (R@SNP) to induce tumor cell senescence; then, SNP loaded with brefeldin A (B@SNP) is used to trigger ER stress. By sequential therapy, R@SNP disrupts the cytoskeleton of 4T1 tumor cells to eliminate ER-targeting barriers and remodels the tumor immune microenvironment; B@SNP boosts ER-targeting efficiency and triggers intense ER stress. Collectively, such time engine nanosystem achieves excellent ER accumulation and antimetastatic efficacy in 4T1 tumor–bearing mice, providing an innovative perspective for subcellular delivery and tumor treatment.

title: Enhancer binding kinetics explain transcription factor hub formation
abstract: Transcription factors (TFs) form dynamic, high-concentration clusters, condensates, or hubs, proposed to increase TF binding frequency at target enhancers. However, how enhancer sequence shapes hub properties remains unclear. We developed a live imaging–based framework to quantify the spatiotemporal relationship between TF hubs and actively transcribed genes in live Drosophila embryos. Examining hubs formed by the TF Dorsal across enhancers with defined binding site composition, we find that hub enrichment and persistence scale with the number of Dorsal binding motifs. However, these hub properties do not predict transcriptional bursts for a given enhancer. Combining quantitative imaging with computational modeling, we show that Dorsal hub formation can be explained by TF-DNA binding kinetics alone. These findings support a model in which TF hubs emerge from enhancer-encoded TF-DNA interactions rather than higher-order regulatory assemblies.

title: Chromatin interaction landscape of epimorphic regeneration in teleost fish
abstract: Reorganization of chromatin architecture—including chromatin loops, topologically associating domains (TADs), and A/B compartments—has been increasingly linked to development and cell differentiation. However, how chromatin architecture reorganizes during the shift from homeostasis to regeneration remains poorly characterized. Here, we used zebrafish fin regeneration as a model to systematically investigate, via micro-C, the chromatin architecture associated with blastema formation. Our analyses unveiled that the alteration of chromatin looping upon amputation was dominant compared with that of TADs and compartments. Genes directly linked to injury-altered loop interactions, including essential regeneration regulators, were mainly related to morphogenesis and cell division. A side-by-side comparison between zebrafish and African killifish uncovered conserved and species-specific chromatin reorganization following injury. Notably, perturbing injury-altered loop interactions at the il11a locus suppressed its expression and impaired fin regeneration efficiency. Further, CTCF/CTCFL and Atf7 binding motifs were the top shared motifs enriched in regeneration-altered loop anchors. Our study uncovers the landscape of chromatin interactions during fin regeneration.

title: Extracellular matrix–targeted TNC-scFv armoring enhances CAR T cell persistence and antitumor activity in solid tumors
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor T cell (CAR T cell) therapy has shown limited efficacy in solid tumors, largely due to physical and immunosuppressive barriers imposed by the tumor microenvironment (TME). Tenascin-C (TNC), an extracellular matrix protein highly expressed in multiple solid malignancies, contributes to immune exclusion and T cell dysfunction. Here, we engineer an armored CAR T cell platform that locally targets the extracellular matrix by secreting a TNC-specific single-chain variable fragment (TNC-scFv) linked to conventional CAR architecture. TNC-scFv–armored CAR T cells exhibit enhanced cytotoxic activity, improved persistence, and reduced exhaustion in vitro and in xenograft tumor models. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis reveals that TNC targeting reprograms the TME toward a CD8 + T cell–enriched and functionally active immune landscape. In humanized tumor models, TNC-scFv–armored CAR T cells mediate robust antitumor responses with minimal systemic toxicity. This extracellular matrix–targeted armoring framework is compatible with additional immunomodulatory payloads, as illustrated by combinatorial armoring with interleukin-2, which further enhances efficacy while mitigating cytokine-associated toxicity. Together, these results establish extracellular matrix–directed armoring as a generalizable strategy to improve CAR T cell therapy for solid tumors.

title: Carbonic anhydrase VIII regulates IP3R1-dependent Ca 2+ signaling to coordinate insulin secretion and hepatic glucose production
abstract: Intracellular Ca 2+ signaling is essential for glucose-induced insulin secretion (GIIS) and hepatic glucose production (HGP), yet how Ca 2+ dynamics are coordinated across organs remains unclear. Carbonic anhydrase VIII (CA8), an endogenous inhibitor of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptor 1 (IP3R1), was identified as a shared regulator of pancreatic and hepatic glucose metabolism. Using Car8 wdl mice, we showed that CA8 deficiency enhanced GIIS and HGP in vivo and ex vivo. In islets and hepatocytes, CA8 loss augments Ca 2+ oscillations, an effect abolished by IP3R inhibition or Car8 reexpression. Enhanced HGP persists independently of glucagon receptor, PLC, or PKA signaling and occurs without increased IP 1 , indicating heightened IP3R1 sensitivity rather than increased IP 3 production. In hepatocytes, chronic glucagon exposure attenuated acute glucagon responsiveness in a CA8-dependent manner. In obese diabetic mice, CA8 increased in islets but decreased in hepatocytes; hepatic CA8 restoration reduced excessive HGP. Collectively, these findings identify CA8 as a cross-organ regulator of IP3R1-dependent Ca 2+ signaling with translational relevance to diabetes.

title: Magnetic omniconversion: Source-independent molding of magnetostatic fields
abstract: Magnetic fields are constrained by the geometry and location of their sources, limiting the ability to freely tailor their spatial distribution. We introduce a general framework to passively convert the magnetic field generated by arbitrary sources into any prescribed desired field within a finite source-free region. Our method relies on field shaping using linear magnetic materials, enabling source-independent magnetic field molding. We provide the general recipe, analytical and numerical demonstrations for some paradigmatic examples, and a proof-of-concept experiment that validates the idea and materials implementation. This approach enables original possibilities in magnetic shielding, targeted field delivery, advanced imaging technologies, and a broad range of field-control applications.

title: Buffaloed in Brandenburg: Germany’s first brush with foot-and-mouth disease after four decades of freedom
abstract: Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) virus is one of the most feared and most consequential pathogens of livestock worldwide. It can be spread rapidly by the transboundary movement of animals, animal products, and by-products. In January 2025, Germany detected its first FMD outbreak since 1988 in extensively reared water buffalo on a small farm in the state of Brandenburg, directly outside Berlin, the federal capital. Immediate control measures including a standstill for movements of susceptible animals and pre-emptive culling were implemented by the veterinary authorities. Whole-genome sequencing identified the virus as serotype O, topotype ME-SA, lineage SA-2018 and revealed extensive recombination, but cross-neutralization assays suggested good heterologous protection by an O/PanAsia-2 vaccine strain. Epidemiological back-calculation placed the time of virus introduction in late December 2024. Although the entry route remains unresolved, human-associated introduction is most likely. Network analysis revealed minimal farm connectivity, and simulations predicted low potential for onward transmission, which is consistent with the outbreak being ultimately restricted to a single herd. This event underscores the constant and unpredictable risk of introduction of the virus. Early detection through increased awareness and comprehensive differential diagnostics as well as the international collaboration of veterinary services, laboratories, and experts are essential in the face of the global presence of FMD.

title: Long-term immunoprophylaxis by TLR9 ligand mediates macrophage-ILC cross-talk against respiratory viral infection
abstract: Rapid development of host immunity is critical during the emergence of viral outbreaks when vaccines are not yet available. Here, we demonstrate that CpG oligodeoxynucleotide-schizophyllan complex (K3-SPG) induces antigen-independent, long-term protection against lethal respiratory virus infection. A single intranasal administration successfully enhanced host resistance to infection for as long as 100 days posttreatment. Mechanistically, we observed a lung-restricted biphasic innate activation of macrophages and innate lymphoid cells. Early protection was mediated by CD11b + CD11c + macrophages (DP MΦ) and monocyte-derived interstitial macrophages (IMΦ). Late protection was mediated by innate lymphoid cells that were epigenetically reprogrammed, suggesting that two distinct innate immune subsets contribute to the maintenance of disease tolerance in the lung microenvironment. Deficiency of TLR9 or TNF-α abrogated innate activation and protective immunity. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that adjuvant-induced prophylaxis is a promising approach to enhancing host resistance against respiratory virus infection, involving the biphasic cooperation between innate immune cells in the local tissue.

title: Dishevelled-mediated clustering stabilizes Frizzled6 and Vangl2 to establish planar cell polarity in the mammalian skin
abstract: Planar cell polarity (PCP) in epithelia is characterized by the polarized distribution of two opposing, membrane-associated PCP complexes across cell junctions. Transmembrane components of the PCP complex bridge cell junctions and organize into punctate, intercellular assemblies that exhibit a high degree of stability. Here, we define the contributions of the cytoplasmic PCP protein, Dishevelled (Dvl), in the submicrometer scale organization and stability of PCP complexes. Using endogenously tagged fluorescent PCP reporters in the embryonic mouse epidermis, we quantify PCP protein mobility and clustering during polarization. We find that as transmembrane proteins immobilize into puncta, Dvl2/3 coaccumulates with its transmembrane partner Frizzled 6 in a polarized manner and stabilizes clusters of PCP complexes. We identify a previously unknown function for the oligomerizing Dishevelled/Axin (DIX) domain of Dvl3, typically associated with Wnt signaling, in Dvl3 asymmetric localization. These observations underscore a role for Dvl oligomerization in assembly and stabilization of asymmetric PCP puncta.

title: ALIX-dependent small extracellular vesicles from tissue-resident mesenchymal cells regulate pancreatic β cell proliferation in obesity
abstract: Cells throughout the body release small extracellular vesicles (sEVs), including exosomes, that function as modulators of both local and systemic metabolism. Using mice in which ALIX, a key regulator of sEV biogenesis, was selectively deleted in PDGFRα + mesenchymal progenitors (Pα-ALIXKO mice), we demonstrate a critical role for mesenchymal sEV production in metabolic regulation. In high-fat diet–induced obesity, Pα-ALIXKO mice exhibited reduced weight gain and smaller subcutaneous adipocytes compared with control mice. Despite similar insulin sensitivity, these mice showed impaired glucose tolerance, which was associated with reduced pancreatic β cell area and smaller islets. sEVs isolated from conditioned media of knockout (KO)–derived mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) exhibited a reduced capacity to promote β cell proliferation. Furthermore, MSCs isolated from subcutaneous adipose tissue of KO mice showed elevated mRNA expression of inflammatory genes. Together, these findings indicate that ALIX in tissue-resident mesenchymal progenitors is required for pancreatic β cell proliferation and glucose homeostasis in obesity.

title: Wildfires diminish vegetation control on surface runoff
abstract: Wildfires are increasingly reshaping global terrestrial ecosystems, yet their impacts on the fundamental coupling between vegetation and the hydrological cycle remain poorly understood. Here, we present a global-scale assessment of how wildfire disturbances alter the sensitivity of surface runoff to vegetation dynamics using multidecadal satellite observations and reanalysis datasets. We developed a spatially explicit framework to quantify pre- and postfire runoff-vegetation sensitivity across climatic gradients and fire regimes. We show a widespread and systematic weakening of vegetation control on runoff after wildfires, indicating a fundamental decoupling of hydrology-vegetation interactions. This attenuation is notably modulated by aridity and fire intensity, with the most pronounced sensitivity losses occurring in fragile drylands. These findings expose a critical blind spot in traditional hydrological models that overlook disturbance-driven vegetation shifts. Our study provides a mechanistic understanding of how compound climate-fire perturbations accelerate terrestrial water flux instability, suggesting that increasing fire frequency will exacerbate ecosystem vulnerability and threaten water security in a warming world.

title: Hydrogen isotopes reveal water leakage from the core
abstract: Chemical heterogeneities in Earth’s deep mantle may record either preserved primordial reservoirs or later core-mantle exchange, but distinguishing between these origins remains challenging. Hydrogen isotopes offer a sensitive tracer, yet whether magma ocean crystallization could generate a deuterium-depleted deep reservoir has not been quantitatively evaluated. Here, we use machine learning–accelerated path-integral simulations to determine equilibrium hydrogen isotope fractionation between silicate melt and bridgmanite, ringwoodite, and wadsleyite under magma ocean conditions. Incorporating these fractionation factors into a magma ocean crystallization model shows that mineral-melt fractionation is intrinsically weak, producing an essentially homogeneous D/H distribution in the primitive mantle. Magma ocean crystallization therefore cannot generate the extremely low δD values observed in some ocean island basalts. Combined with exceptionally high 3 He/ 4 He ratios, these signatures more plausibly reflect selective transfer of primordial volatiles from Earth’s core, implying sustained volatile exchange across the core-mantle boundary.

title: Multiscale insights into screw dislocation-driven growth mechanisms
abstract: Spiral growth in two-dimensional (2D) materials has conventionally been explained by single screw dislocation mechanisms, yet a complete multiscale understanding remains elusive due to the intricate nature of screw dislocation structures. Here, we present a stabilization approach through metallic transition metal dichalcogenides (m-TMDs) overlayers on spiral semiconducting TMDs (s-TMDs), which enables unprecedentedly robust atomic-resolution imaging of screw dislocations in cross-sectional van der Waals heterostructures. Our multiscale investigations identify nanoscale substrate undulations as critical nucleation sites for screw dislocations and uncover a multi-screw dislocation-driven (MSDD) growth paradigm, characterized by periodic stress stripes with linear densities approaching ∼10 6 cm −1 . Furthermore, we establish that dislocation interactions govern stacking sequence reconstruction, while the kinetic competition among multiple screw dislocations determines the ultimate spiral architectures. These insights fundamentally transform our understanding of defect-mediated growth in 2D materials.

title: SMCHD1 is a target for gene activation therapy to treat Prader-Willi syndrome
abstract: Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS) is a neurodevelopmental disorder caused by loss of expression from the active paternal allele at an imprinted cluster on chromosome 15. Current treatments address individual symptoms rather than the underlying cause of disease. Because all patients preserve a normal but epigenetically silenced maternal copy of these genes, activation of this copy offers a potential disease-modifying therapy. Here, we investigated the epigenetic regulator SMCHD1. First, we demonstrated that SMCHD1 represses the PWS locus in both mice and humans, supporting its relevance as a therapeutic target. Second, we found that SMCHD1 represses the entire PWS locus in neural lineages, extending its previously known role beyond only part of the cluster. Deleting Smchd1 after early development in vivo activated PWS genes in disease-relevant mouse tissues including hypothalamus and improved phenotypes in a PWS mouse model. Despite broader genome-wide binding, postearly development targeting of SMCHD1 appeared remarkably safe, supporting its potential for gene activation therapy for PWS.

title: Erratum for the Research Article “Microenvironment-driven transformable self-assembly nanoplatform enables spatiotemporal remodeling for rheumatoid arthritis therapy” by C. Hu et al.
Erratum for the Research Article “Regulation of body length and bone mass by Gpr126/Adgrg6” by P. Sun et al .
Erratum for the Research Article “CEMs-SELEX: DNAzyme-powered de novo biomarker discovery and noninvasive cancer diagnosis” by W. Cui et al.
Erratum for the Research Article “The pore size of mesoporous silica nanoparticles regulates their antigen delivery efficiency”
Erratum for the Research Article “A novel β-catenin/BCL9 complex inhibitor blocks oncogenic Wnt signaling and disrupts cholesterol homeostasis in colorectal cancer”
Mitochondrial carbonic anhydrase–VB inhibition rescues brain endothelial stress and memory in Alzheimer’s disease models
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a devastating neurodegenerative disorder with no effective cure, characterized by the cerebral parenchymal and vascular accumulation of aggregated amyloid-β (Aβ) and hyperphosphorylated tau. Cerebrovascular and mitochondria dysfunction are early causal events in the progression of AD. Previous studies support that inhibiting carbonic anhydrases (CAs) may prevent mitochondrial and cerebrovascular dysfunction in AD models. Here, we selectively target the mitochondrial CA isoform CA-VB by pharmacological and genetic manipulation in human cerebral microvascular endothelial cells (hCMEC), and we confirm the protective effects of the CA-V inhibitor in AD mice. CA-V inhibition and CA-VB KO prevent Aβ induced mitochondria-mediated endothelial apoptosis, loss of barrier resistance, and hCMEC inflammatory activation. Strikingly, CA-V inhibition also mitigates caspase activation and endothelial cell activation in the brains of 3xTg AD mice, resulting in preserved memory function. Our results demonstrate that selective CA-V inhibition is an effective and promising strategy against AD-mediated cerebrovascular pathology, neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment.

title: How inequality became durable before states: Evidence from 6000 years in the Central Plain of China
abstract: How did durable inequality emerge before the rise of states? Drawing on a synthesis of previously published mortuary data from more than 2300 burials, together with isotopic, zooarchaeological, and osteological data spanning nearly 6000 years (7000 to 1500 BCE) in the prehistoric Central Plain of China, we reconstruct long-term patterns of relational mortuary inequality. We show that inequality followed a strongly nonlinear trajectory and cannot be explained primarily by agricultural intensification or population scale. Instead, substantial disparities were structured by differential positions within social-relational networks that mediated access to labor, resources, and symbolic capital. Transformations in subsistence, the rise of mobile and appropriable wealth, and escalating conflict reorganized these networks, concentrating ritual and political-military power and technological control. Early states stabilized rather than created these preexisting disparities by institutionalizing control over resources, violence, and network-based access. These findings highlight the central role of social networks in shaping durable inequality before formal state institutions.

title: Macrophage- or neutrophil-expressed UPP1 drives tumor growth and immune suppression in the tumor microenvironment
abstract: Uridine phosphorylase 1 (UPP1) has recently emerged as a metabolic regulator with critical roles in tumor cell biology. However, its expression pattern and functional significance in nonmalignant components of the tumor microenvironment (TME) remain largely unexplored. Here, we performed a comprehensive pan-cancer single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealing that UPP1 is highly expressed not only in tumor cells but also in tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and neutrophils (TANs). Clinically, UPP1 expression in TAMs and TANs correlates with poor prognosis and diminished response to immunotherapy across multiple cancer types. Mechanistically, UPP1 up-regulation could be driven by NF-κB signaling. Functionally, UPP1 reprograms macrophages toward a tumor-promoting phenotype, characterized by enhanced glycolysis, ATP-adenosine signaling activation, and increased production of immunosuppressive cytokines such as granulocyte colony-stimulating factor. In neutrophils, UPP1 also supports TAN polarization, influences neutrophil extracellular trap release, and contributes to broad immunosuppressive remodeling. In vivo, targeting UPP1 in macrophages or neutrophils reprograms the immune landscape and restrains tumor progression. Together, our findings uncover a previously underappreciated role of UPP1 in nonmalignant immune populations and establish it as a key immune mediator within the TME, offering a potentially promising therapeutic target for enhancing antitumor immunity.

title: Rising global population coexposure to heatwaves and landscape fire-sourced air pollution
abstract: Landscape fires are increasingly threatening public health by causing substantial fire-sourced air pollution (SFAP), with risks amplified during heatwaves. We investigated the global spatial, temporal, and sociodemographic distribution of the population coexposure to heatwaves and SFAP from 2000 to 2019. We found that 52.4% of populated areas and 55.9% of the global population experienced increasing coexposure. On average, 916 million people per year were exposed to at least one coexposure day, increasing by 287 million people per decade. The global annual average exposed days per person was 1.3 days, rising from 1.0 days in 2000–2009 to 1.7 days in 2010–2019. Coexposure person-days increased by 5.5 billion per decade, of which 70.5% was attributable to increasing coexposure intensity and 29.5% to population growth. Countries with a low human development index (HDI) experienced the highest coexposure days per person and the greatest increases. These findings provide high-resolution data to inform health impact assessments and target mitigation and adaptation strategies.

title: Learning to infer transitively on a mental line in premotor cortex
abstract: Transitive inference (TI) is a form of deductive reasoning that enables the derivation of unknown relationships among premises. It is hypothesized that this cognitive process relies on mapping stimuli onto a “mental line,” a linear workspace organized by arbitrarily assigned ranks. However, its neural basis remains unclear: Does this mental line have a neural correlate and how is it learned? This study investigates the role of dorsal premotor cortex (PMd) in encoding the hypothesized mental line as monkeys acquire item relationships for motor decisions. Findings reveal that PMd multiunit activity organizes along a theoretically predicted direction, supporting a geometrical model that explains behavior. Moreover, a learning process is observed, where the mental line rotates to align with motor planning.

title: Plasmonic metasurface microfluidic accelerates redox reactions for rapid phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing
abstract: Electron-accepting chain reactions play crucial roles in diagnostics for bacterial infections, from nucleic acid amplification for bacterial identification to metabolic assays for phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing. When coupled with redox mediators, these reactions can be interrogated using an electroanalytical method. We demonstrate kinetic acceleration of loop-mediated isothermal amplification–based identification and resazurin-based phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility profiling through enhanced electromagnetic fields and modulated hot electron injection at the multilayered plasmonic metasurface-fluidic interface. We systematically investigate rounded versus sharp-apex plasmonic architectures, quantifying near-field magnitude and decay to identify geometries that maximize kinetic amplification under electrochemical readout. This approach is further combined with machine learning–assisted Gaussian fitting to improve data quantification and interpretation. Across diverse bacterial species, we achieved rapid identification with no cross-reactivity and phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing without overnight culture. In a prospective pilot clinical study of urine specimens directly from patients with suspected urinary tract infections, we observe high accuracy and strong essential and categorical agreement with standard clinical microbiology assays for bacterial identification and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

title: Comprehensive characterization of transposable element expression reveals regulatory circuitry and clinical implications in cancers
abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) constitute nearly half of the human genome and have crucial roles in regulatory networks and clinical utility in cancers. However, the expression profiles at a single-element resolution remain unexplored. By integrating multiomics data from ∼10,000 samples and 1000 cancer cell lines, we established an expression atlas of 95,512 individual TEs across 980 subfamilies. Transcription factors and RNA binding proteins that are broadly associated with expressed TEs were involved in cancer-related signaling pathways (e.g., MYC activity). We identified 264,252 TEs as putative cis-regulatory elements associated with oncogenic pathways such as inflammatory response. We analyzed alterations in TE expression in tumors and their associations with clinical relevance and responses to more than 1000 anticancer drugs. Last, we developed the Atlas of Transposon Expression in Cancer (ATEC), a TE data portal enabling users to explore TE expression patterns, putative regulatory networks, and clinical significance. Overall, this study established a comprehensive resource for TEs across cancer types.

title: Local control of Cre-regulated genetic modeling in vivo using wireless implantable optoelectronics
abstract: Effective modeling of chronic human diseases in vivo requires precise spatiotemporal regulation of molecular processes at defined tissue locations. Optogenetic and optoelectronic tools can provide such control but targeting internal organs such as the lungs remain challenging. To address this, we developed E-LightR-Cre recombinase, enabling precise, spatially restricted gene activation with no dark-state activity and robust blue light responsiveness. To achieve local activation of E-LightR-Cre in specific organ sites, we engineered wireless, fully implantable optoelectronic devices enabling focal illumination of murine lungs with no discernible organ damage. The size of the activated area is controlled by modulating light intensity and duration. Using implanted optoelectronic devices, we activated E-LightR-Cre in a selected area of mouse lungs and achieved local regulation of targeted genes. Light-regulated expression of the oncogenic KRas-G12D mutant in mouse lungs induced local formation of oncogenic lesions. These results show that our protein engineering and adaptable optoelectronic approaches enable facile application of optogenetic tools for locally controlled disease modeling in vivo.

title: An inspiration-off attractor supports the robust and flexible control of breathing
abstract: Breathing is a fundamental motor rhythm necessary to sustain life. The rhythm and pattern of breathing arises from the coordination of a rostrocaudally extended ventral respiratory column (VRC) in the medulla. Although recurrent excitation is sufficient for rhythmic bursting in reduced in vitro preparations, comparatively less is understood about how inhibition and excitation interact with feedback circuits to generate the breathing rhythm in vivo. Here, we expand on the classical “inspiratory-off switch” model that inhibitory signaling from lung stretch afferent pathways plays a critical role in generating the breathing rhythm in vivo. We perform high-density extracellular recordings along the length of the VRC during optogenetic and physiological manipulations and apply computational analyses to characterize how these perturbations govern low-dimensional neural dynamics. We show that stimulation of GABAergic afferents of the nucleus of the solitary tract advance or delay breathing in a manner similar to, but quantitatively distinct from, inhibition local to the VRC. We use generative dynamical models to show that inhibitory activity controls respiratory activity through transient stabilization of an attractive region of the low-dimensional manifold corresponding to expiration. Together, these results propose an “inspiratory-off attractor” model that underlies network level control of breathing in vivo.

title: Global conservation additionality hindered by persisting fishing pressure in marine protected areas
abstract: Marine protected areas (MPAs) are the cornerstone of global marine conservation strategies. Yet, their capacity to achieve conservation gains (i.e., conservation additionality) hinges on the decrease in human threats to biodiversity within their boundary, a feature rarely measured or reported. Here, we test a central but underexamined question in global conservation policy: Have MPA implementations actually reduced within-boundary fishing pressure, currently the main direct human threat to marine biodiversity? Using a stratified before-after-control-impact approach, we investigated 861 MPAs of varying levels of protection across all ocean basins, representing half of global MPA coverage, and found that most implementations were not followed by decreases in industrial fishing effort. Protection levels strongly predicted the direction and magnitude of relative changes in fishing effort after implementation. Only fully protected areas were associated with significant decreases in fishing effort within boundaries. Highly protected areas were only associated with lower rates of increase in fishing effort within compared to outside boundaries. Both fully and highly protected areas were implemented in areas experiencing initial low fishing effort, reducing the overall abatement in fishing effort achieved. Conversely, areas with higher initial fishing effort tended to be attributed to MPAs with low levels of protection, also limiting abatement. Larger MPAs were associated with greater decreases in fishing effort, while time since implementation had no significant effect. Complementing targets of protection coverage and protection levels with conservation additionality targets, such as pressure abatement, could shift incentives from quantity to effectiveness of interventions and ensure positive biodiversity conservation outcomes.

title: Photomapping electrically coupled networks of the mature thalamus and cortex
abstract: Electrical synapses are expressed ubiquitously across the brain and are crucial components of active neural circuitry and connectomes. Identification of coupled networks in living tissue is limited by technical demands of multiplexed recordings, and no dyes, fluorescent reporters, or genetic labels can now fill the gap. We introduce a novel method of identifying and quantifying electrical synapses, opto-δ L , that combines focal photostimulation of soma-targeted opsins with a spike timing–based computation for the strength of electrical synapses to rapidly measure and map electrically coupled networks in vitro. We leverage opto-δ L to show that coupled networks of the mature thalamic reticular nucleus extend as far as 100 micrometers, synapse promiscuously across genetic subtypes of neurons, and couple one to four neighboring neurons to each recorded hub cell. We applied opto-δ L to cortical networks, where we found that somatostatin neurons were more strongly and prevalently coupled. These results highlight the broad potential of opto-δ L to interrogate the identity and roles of electrical synapses in circuitry, behavior, and cognition.

title: The network structure of the urban revolution
abstract: Long-distance interaction has deep prehistoric roots, but the networks that emerged during the Urban Revolution were unprecedented in scale and organization. How early cities sustained this extensive connectivity in the absence of formal markets or centralized states remains a fundamental question. Focusing on the Uruk Expansion in Mesopotamia (ca. 3900 to 3000 BCE), we assemble the largest spatial dataset currently available and reconstruct transportation networks across three successive phases. Using network analysis, we show that an initially dendritic, river-based system evolved into modular regional clusters and ultimately into a more integrated structure linked by selective long-distance shortcuts. This transformation reduced dependence on key intermediaries and generated small world–like patterns combining strong local cohesion with efficient system-wide reach. These results demonstrate that decentralized interaction processes, supported in part by mobile intermediary communities, played a central role in sustaining early urban connectivity.

title: Reversible Atlantic overturning despite continued Greenland ice sheet melt
abstract: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is considered vulnerable to irreversible weakening or collapse under global warming and related Greenland ice sheet (GrIS) melt, yet its resilience to either forcing remains poorly constrained. Here, we use a carbon dioxide emission–driven Earth system model with an interactive GrIS to assess AMOC reversibility under a range of idealized carbon dioxide emission pathways that produce near-linear global warming up to 10 kelvins (K), stabilization across 1.5 to 9 K, and subsequent cooling. We find that although the AMOC reaches threshold-defined collapsed states, these do not represent dynamical tipping in this model: The overturning weakens quasi-linearly with global mean temperature increase yet consistently and promptly recovers under cooling. In contrast, GrIS mass loss accelerates with warming, continues through stabilizations, and is only slowed by cooling, committing the planet to long-term sea level rise. These results reveal contrasting resilience across climate system components: Under transient carbon dioxide forcing, AMOC strength remains dynamically reversible despite continued Greenland meltwater input, whereas the GrIS is locked into persistent decline. Our findings underscore the urgency of rapid emission cuts to limit climate overshoot, AMOC weakening, and irreversible ice sheet loss.

title: A B1 SINE element within the mouse Malat1 long noncoding RNA acts as an internal ribosome entry site mediating micropeptide translation
abstract: In most cells, Malat1 long noncoding RNA localizes to the nucleus where it affects splicing and chromatin function. In mouse neurons, Malat1 is exported to the cytoplasm where it is translated to generate the M1 micropeptide. Here, we characterize an internal ribosome entry site (IRES) required for M1 translation that is sufficient to induce cap-independent expression of a downstream open reading frame. In vivo chemical probing and structural modeling defined a three-stem-loop RNA secondary structure that encompasses the active IRES segment and coincides with a mouse B1 SINE (short interspersed element) repetitive element. In affinity purification experiments, a minimal IRES/B1 RNA selectively bound ribosomal subunits, translation factors, and the known IRES cofactors Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1. Depletion of Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1 inhibited IRES-dependent translation of the reporter and expression of the endogenous M1 peptide. Our study identifies an unexpected functional unit hidden within a widely studied long noncoding RNA.

title: Immune biomarkers of response and resistance to ipilimumab and nivolumab in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
abstract: Immune checkpoint therapies have shown limited efficacy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). The AMADEUS prostate expansion cohort (NCT03651271) evaluated the efficacy, safety, and biomarkers of escalating ipilimumab doses combined with nivolumab. Patients received ipilimumab 1 milligram per kilogram (mg/kg) + nivolumab 360 mg (I1+N360), ipilimumab 3 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg (I3+N1), or ipilimumab 5 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg (I5+N1). Coprimary endpoints were 6-month disease control rate (DCR) and changes in tumoral CD8 percentage. Thirty-two patients were enrolled. DCRs were 33% (4 of 12) for I1+N360, 20% (1 of 5) for I3+N1, and 20% (3 of 15) for I5+N1. Across cohorts, tumoral CD8 percentage increased by a median of 5.0%. Although higher ipilimumab doses were tolerable, I1+N360 achieved similar disease control and immune activation with a more favorable safety profile. Early disease progression was associated with increased expression of a TREM2-associated myeloid gene signature, which was also significantly enriched in two independent prostate cancer datasets.

title: Deep learning reveals ecological decoupling and rate heterogeneity in Hymenoptera wing evolution
abstract: Quantifying biomorphological evolution and integrating phenotypic data into large-scale ecological and evolutionary studies are often limited by the scalability, subjectivity, and poor interpretability of existing methods. We introduce HAIKA (Hierarchical Attention-based Interpretable K-dimensional Autoencoder), a self-supervised residual channel-attention autoencoder that extracts continuous morphological representations from unlabeled standardized images and highlights the image regions that contribute to those representations. Applied to insect forewings across broad pterygote lineages, HAIKA outperformed most baseline deep learning models and conventional descriptors in clustering, dimensionality reduction, and morphological embedding. When applied to Hymenoptera (i.e., ants, bees, and wasps), the HAIKA-derived continuous characters improved morphology-based phylogenetic reconstruction and illuminated the evolutionary dynamics of wing shape and venation. Our results reveal that wing morphological evolution in Hymenoptera proceeds at decoupled rates across shape and venation modules and is not consistently aligned with key ecological transitions such as parasitoidism or eusociality. HAIKA provides a scalable, image-based route for phenotypic analyses, broadly applicable across diverse taxa and to both 2D and 3D datasets.

title: Polyclonal breast milk–derived secretory IgA confers broad antiviral protection against multiple respiratory viruses
abstract: Passive immunization is an important tool for protecting individuals with primary immune deficiencies from infectious diseases and offers a rapid response strategy for protecting vulnerable populations, particularly during the interval between pathogen emergence and vaccine deployment. Current approaches rely on intravenous delivery of IgG-enriched plasma or monoclonal antibodies, which limits accessibility, scalability, and effectiveness at mucosal surfaces, the primary entry point for respiratory viruses. Here, we tested LCTG-001, a polyclonal secretory IgA preparation derived from pooled human breast milk, to address these limitations. LCTG-001 demonstrated broad antiviral activity against clinically relevant respiratory viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, and influenza A virus. LCTG-001 effectively recognized both group 1 and group 2 influenza A subtypes, including the highly pathogenic H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b, and engaged nonneutralizing effector mechanisms such as neuraminidase inhibition and neutrophil activation. When administered intranasally, LCTG-001 conferred complete protection against influenza A challenge in both immunocompetent and antibody-deficient murine models, preventing morbidity and mortality through a transient early reduction in viral burden followed by sustained improvements in lung pathology and lung barrier integrity. These findings highlight the potential of breast milk–derived secretory IgA as a scalable, mucosa-targeted passive immunization strategy capable of addressing both endemic and emerging respiratory viral threats.

title: SPRIZ (CCDC127) protein conserved in deuterostome animals is a rigid OMM–IMM tether that locally sets mitochondrial IMS volume
abstract: The double-membrane nature of mitochondria generates an intermembrane volume through which ions, reactive oxygen species, and metabolites must flux to reach the matrix or cytosol, but whether this volume is a genetically specified structure remains unknown. We identify SPRIZ (spatial regulator of the intermembrane zone), the product of Ccdc127 , a gene conserved across deuterostome animals. SPRIZ assembles into an ∼18-nanometer homodimeric tether anchored in the outer mitochondrial membrane (OMM) and inserted into the inner mitochondrial membrane (IMM) through vertebrate-specific hydrophobic loops, physically spacing the two membranes and setting local intermembrane volume. Cryo-electron tomography of native mitochondria revealed rod-like densities spanning the intermembrane space (IMS), consistent with SPRIZ’s predicted rigid coiled-coil architecture and membrane-spanning topology. In mouse liver, two-dimensional morphometry measured ∼3-fold expansion of IMS area with SPRIZ and ∼5.5-fold with lengthened mitochondrial artificial increaser of the IMS (MARTINI); 3D electron tomography confirmed MARTINI’s greater OMM–IMM separation and normalized IMS volume. This expansion was functionally validated by increased 14 C-mannitol accessibility to the IMS and by impaired mitochondrial Ca 2+ uptake. Constitutive Ccdc127/SPRIZ knockout produced viable mice and, in liver mitochondria, preserved overall ultrastructure but caused modest IMS expansion, consistent with loss of local OMM–IMM constraints that stabilize membrane geometry at discrete sites. We therefore identify IMS volume as a genetically encoded and tunable architectural parameter of vertebrate mitochondria. In this model, SPRIZ is a molecular spacing system that locally sets OMM–IMM separation, shaping the environment through which metabolites, ions, and signals diffuse and establishing local gradients within the IMS.

title: Spectral tuning and signaling of diverse and far red–sensitive rhodopsins in mantis shrimp eyes
abstract: Stomatopod crustaceans (mantis shrimps) have extraordinary eyes with unmatched visual rhodopsin diversity, but their potential for broad color detection remains unclear. Here, we report that 17 rhodopsins, mostly from the midband eye region, are involved in color sensing and functionally diverse signaling via Gq/Gi coupling and describe the underlying mechanisms of spectral tuning. Two mid-wavelength rhodopsins preferentially absorb blue light and a majority of long-wavelength opsins absorb in the green range, but three absorb light beyond 600 nanometers, representing exquisite far red–sensitive animal rhodopsins. Several blue and red rhodopsins exhibit photoreversibility with opposite spectral shifts explained by retinal binding interactions, revealing unrecognized photochemical flexibility in stomatopod photoreception. Row-specific spectral sensitivity results from combining carotenoid filters with multiple individually tuned rhodopsins, altogether extending broad vision to the far-red spectrum.

title: A fast and frugal Gaussian boson sampling emulator
abstract: Classical algorithms have successfully reproduced expectation values of observables for certain quantum circuits using off-the-shelf computing resources; however, matching the performance of the most advanced quantum devices on sampling problems typically incurs extreme memory and computational costs, restricting such simulations to only a handful of supercomputers worldwide. In this work, we demonstrate a classical simulation outperforming Gaussian boson sampling experiments of 100 modes on established benchmark tests using a single central processing unit (CPU) or graphics processing unit (GPU). Being embarrassingly parallelizable, a small number of CPUs or GPUs allows us to match previous sampling rates that required more than 100 GPUs. We believe that algorithmic and implementation improvements have the potential to generalize our tools to photocounting and pseudo–photon number–resolving scenarios and larger system sizes. Last, most of the innovations in our tools remain valid for generic probability distributions over binary variables, rendering them potentially applicable to the simulation of qubit-based sampling problems and creating classical surrogates for classical-quantum algorithms.

title: Ice nucleation by kaolinite: Morphology shapes the size dependence of ice nucleation active sites on dust particles
abstract: Mineral dusts are the most important type of ice-nucleating particles and play a key role in cloud formation and climate. Their activity is commonly assumed to scale with particle surface area, yet whether this assumption holds across particle sizes remains unverified. Here, we quantify size-dependent ice nucleation activity using compositionally pure, size-segregated kaolinite (KGa-1b). Ice nucleation active site (INAS) densities were determined for size classes from submicron to 48 μm, revealing two distinct ice-nucleation regimes. At low temperatures (∼240 K), INAS density per surface area is independent of particle size. In contrast, at warm temperatures (∼260 K), particles of 6 to 12 μm exhibit the highest INAS densities, up to two orders of magnitude greater than smaller particles and nonsize-selected bulk samples. Linking these results to particle morphology indicates that well-aligned, multilayered platelet edges provide the continuous hydroxylated surfaces required for efficient ice nucleation. Our findings demonstrate that morphology can modulate particle size–dependent ice nucleation, highlighting limitations of simple surface area–based parameterizations.

title: Ultrasound-driven electronically programmable microbubbles
abstract: Ultrasound-actuated microbubbles have served as efficient microscale engines demonstrating wireless actuation, simplified robotic architectures, and rapid response. Despite recent advances, a limitation of many microbubble technologies is that they use passive capturing of bubbles. The lack of control over bubble placement and size hinders the ability to individually address specified bubbles, a feature that would be important for performing multiple functions. Here, we present an on-chip bubble customization platform that enables active control of individual microbubbles. Instead of trapping bubbles, we purposely generate them via electrolysis on electrode arrays. The bubbles, when actuated by an external ultrasound input, create a variety of programmed flows ranging from streaming due to volumetric oscillation of a single bubble to diverse symmetry-broken directional flows when multiple bubbles interact. The bubble configuration can also be altered by simply increasing the electrolysis voltage on specified electrodes to detach the unneeded bubbles. We find that in this regime, when coupled to acoustic oscillations, we can generate a distinct bubble shooting flow pattern whose flow direction is selectively controlled by the incident ultrasound frequency. Collectively, the active bubble reconfiguration ability unlocks a range of previously inaccessible acoustofluidic functions in a single device with unprecedented controllability.

title: From scrap to prime: Designing high-performance alloys from dirty feedstocks with machine learning
abstract: Producing alloys from recycled metals via secondary synthesis can markedly cut energy use, greenhouse-gas emissions, and dependence on scarce, strategically important elements relative to primary routes. The central obstacle is the feedstock itself: Scrap is chemically heterogeneous and unpredictable, a “dirty” mix whose impurities typically embrittle materials. Conventional strategies address this challenge by diluting impurities through the addition of virgin material, thereby restricting scrap utilization, limiting microstructural design freedom, and undermining cost and sustainability benefits. Here, we introduce a fundamentally different, data-driven paradigm that deliberately reverses a five-millennia-old metallurgical injunction: Rather than purifying the alloy, we design the alloy to accommodate and exploit its contaminants. Using a model ductile iron representative of 120 million metric tons of heavily contaminated scrap, we couple experiments with deep-neural-network optimization to identify chemically robust, impurity-tolerant processing windows. The resulting “dirty” irons retain ductility and strength by integrating impurity effects into a purposeful microstructure, rather removing them. The approach achieves complete recyclability, an 8.1% reduction in manufacturing cost, and mechanical gains of up to 15.2% in ultimate tensile strength and 73.2% in elongation at fracture. Crucially, it overcomes the canonical strength-ductility trade-off while enabling far greater scrap utilization and material circularity. By endowing alloys with a practical “gene of scrap compatibility,” this strategy reframes alloy design for a resource-constrained future and advances a mass-conserving circular economy for metals.

title: Humans experienced abrupt environmental changes at White Sands during the Last Glacial Maximum
abstract: Expanded excavations at White Sands National Park have unearthed 20 stratigraphic horizons containing in situ human footprints, megafaunal trackways, and linear features created by travois. Advances in radiocarbon dating of conifer pollen, combined with ages of aquatic seeds, refines the chronology of the footprint-bearing sequence to between 23.5 and 21.7 thousand years ago (ka). Biomarker, pollen, and stratigraphic evidence indicate a complete overturning of the environment from a perennial lake to a playa and capture a large aridification episode coincident with Dansgaard-Oeschger event 2 at 23.2 ka, which shrank pluvial Lake Otero and allowed people to traverse the former shoreline area for nearly two millennia. This well-dated and highly resolved paleoclimate record provides compelling evidence that humans in North America experienced marked environmental changes during the Last Glacial Maximum.

title: Highlights from an early base camp in Beringia 13,800 years ago: Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ and the Late Pleistocene peopling of Alaska
abstract: Human dispersal across the Bering Land Bridge (BLB) was a key event in the peopling of the Americas, but Beringia’s archaeological record remains poorly understood. In response, the Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ site in interior Alaska has been the focus of a multi-disciplinary study since 2016. The site contains three archaeological components dating to the Late Pleistocene, 13.8, 13, and 12.7 thousand years ago. The oldest component yielded an expressive array of cultural remains, including a unique hafted-biface form, osseous tools, diverse fauna, and well-preserved activity areas, a record unparalleled for this age in Beringia. Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ represents the earliest known Nenana Complex occupation east of the BLB, and its distinct hafted-biface form occurs in coeval sites west of the BLB, providing an important trans-Beringian cultural link. Although not Beringia’s oldest site, Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ reveals important information about Late Glacial peopling and settling-in behavior in this far northern setting.

title: Rapid coral bleaching recovery via symbiont transfer from healthy corals
abstract: Coral bleaching, the temperature-induced loss of dinoflagellate symbionts, is a major driver of global coral reef decline. Although corals can regain symbionts through repopulation of residual symbionts or via environmental acquisition, these processes are often too slow to prevent coral mortality. Mechanisms that enable rapid and effective symbiont reintroduction leading to full recovery remain largely unknown. Here, we demonstrate coral bleaching recovery through contact-mediated transfer of symbionts from healthy corals using small coral fragments. We show that symbiont transfer is rapid, occurring over days to weeks, and highly efficient, with only brief physical contact with healthy corals required. A single week of contact, and in some cases as few as 3 days, provides sufficient symbionts to initiate sustained and full self-recovery. By 1 week, symbiont population doubling time is approximately 4 days, up to an order of magnitude faster than most recovery times for corals in the field. We identify tissue fusion as the mechanism enabling directional symbiont transfer from healthy to bleached coral tissue. As a result, contact-dependent recovery is restricted to corals of the same genet, whereas heterologous genet pairings trigger antagonistic interactions. However, symbiont transfer via polyp uptake occurs immediately upon contact in both same-genet and mixed-genet pairings, revealing an additional, slower pathway for symbiont transfer that is insufficient on its own to support colony recovery. Collectively, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized natural process for efficiently reintroducing symbionts to bleached corals, providing a foundation for research into potential recovery interventions.

title: Sustainable solar water purification: Exploring the structural advantages of higher plants
abstract: Solar vapor generation is a promising technique for water purification, although the development of efficient and sustainable systems for practical use remains challenging. Here, we introduce a higher plant–derived evaporator, leveraging the structural advantages of plants and the synergistic integration of multiple components, including carbon black–coated ultrathin wood slices with perforated pores, nanocellulose aerogel, and vertically aligned wheat straws. This configuration facilitates low-tortuosity water transport within the internal framework while promoting interfacial evaporation at its surface. Under 1 sun, the evaporator achieved an evaporation rate of up to 3.2 kilograms per square meter (kg m −2 ) per hour. The material’s scalability and the capability to continuously collect clean water in outdoor environments were successfully demonstrated. Outdoors, under a solar intensity of 0.5 to 0.9 sun, the assembled device achieved a daily fresh water yield of up to 10.9 kg m −2 from seawater. With highly accessible renewable raw materials, low production cost, and exceptional water purification efficiency, this cost-effective solar evaporator is edge closer to viable, real-world applications.

title: Integrative multi-omics reveals CUL4B as a modulator of macrophage pyroptosis and innate defense against Staphylococcus aureus
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus (SA) causes a broad range of invasive human diseases, increasingly complicated by antibiotic resistance. Macrophages (MΦ) play a central role in innate immunity, yet key aspects of their interaction with SA remain incompletely understood because of the pathogen’s diverse immune evasion strategies. Using multi-omics and systems-level analytics, we identified the E3 ubiquitin ligase cullin 4B (CUL4B) as a host factor that modulates MΦ responses to SA infection. CRISPR-mediated deletion of CUL4B in human THP-1 MΦ enhanced intracellular bacterial killing, reduced cell death, decreased caspase-1 activation, and lowered interleukin-1β production, consistent with altered inflammasome signaling. In a murine methicillin-resistant SA (MRSA) pneumonia model, CUL4B deficiency improved pulmonary bacterial clearance, reduced bacteremia, and decreased inflammatory tissue injury. Whole-lung and serum proteomics further revealed increased antimicrobial protein abundance and reduced markers of inflammatory damage. Together, these findings identify CUL4B as a regulator of MΦ inflammatory responses during MRSA infection and suggest a potential host-directed pathway that could be leveraged to improve outcomes against this major pathogen.

title: A transcriptional cofactor GRIP1 drives PPARγ DNA binding and p300-dependent enhancer activity during homeostatic macrophage polarization
abstract: Homeostatic macrophages maintain tissue health and resolve inflammation. Upon sustained exposure to type II cytokine IL4, transcription factors STAT6, KLF4, EGR2 and a ligand-regulated nuclear receptor PPARγ orchestrate the M2 IL4 ‘polarization’, marked by enhancer RNA (eRNA) production near multiple M2 genes. The mechanisms of enhancer activation by unliganded PPARγ are poorly understood. We interrogated cofactor requirements for PPARγ-driven gene expression in M2 IL4 , including those lacking PPARγ or a ligand-dependent nuclear receptor coregulator NCoA2/GRIP1 vs. macrophages treated with the PPARγ agonist rosiglitazone. As expected, rosiglitazone activated conventional PPARγ targets; GRIP1 deletion blunted their induction and depleted GRIP1-interacting histone acetyltransferase p300 from PPARγ-bound sites. Surprisingly, GRIP1 colocalized with unliganded PPARγ in M0 and M2 IL4 , and GRIP1 ablation dramatically reduced genome-wide DNA binding of PPARγ itself while promoting broad deposition of CTCF insulator. Functionally, GRIP1 deletion mirrored PPARγ deficiency, establishing GRIP1 as a central regulator of unliganded PPARγ DNA binding, required for both eRNA and mRNA transcription of PPARγ targets in homeostatic macrophages.

title: SRF3 couples cellular iron homeostasis and defense responses through ubiquitin-dependent nano-organization
abstract: Iron homeostasis is a central component of host defense responses. In mammals, iron availability is rapidly adjusted through receptor mediated pathways, whereas it remains unclear how plants regulate iron homeostasis during the earliest stages of immune activation. Here, we identify a rapid iron regulatory mechanism centered on the plasma membrane receptor kinase STRUBBELIG RECEPTOR FAMILY 3 (SRF3), which integrates bacterial immune signaling with ferrous iron homeostasis. Perception of flagellin triggers a burst of reactive oxygen species that induces a rapid and transient depletion of the labile ferrous iron pool. This state promotes SRF3 ubiquitination and clathrin-dependent endocytosis, a process required to restore intracellular ferrous iron levels while dampening immune responses. Using super resolution microscopy, we show that this functional integration relies on ubiquitin dependent nano organization of SRF3 at the plasma membrane, enabling distinct signaling outputs from a single receptor. Thereby, SRF3 modulates both immune signaling and the proliferation of commensal and pathogenic bacteria. Together, our findings uncover a fast-acting iron homeostasis pathway in plants that dynamically couples nutrient availability with immunity, thereby shaping host microbe interactions at the onset of infection.

title: A “Progenitor Cell Ark” hydrogel system for intervertebral disc regeneration via mitochondrial targeting and mitophagy enhancement
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), driven by progenitor cell loss and oxidative stress, remains a major clinical challenge with limited effective regenerative therapies. Here, we present a “Progenitor Cell Ark,” a triple-layered hydrogel microsphere system designed for synergistic cell delivery and microenvironment remediation. The Ark comprises an outer nucleus pulposus progenitor cell (NPPC) layer for cell replenishment, a middle GelMA/HAMA scaffold for support, and an inner SS31-modified ultrasmall Prussian blue nanozyme (SS31-UPN) layer that specifically targets mitochondria to scavenge ROS and promote mitophagy. In vitro, SS31-UPN effectively protected NPPCs from oxidative damage, restored mitochondrial function, and enhanced mitophagy. Critically, in severe IVDD rat models, the Progenitor Cell Ark significantly improved intervertebral disc structure, promoted neo-tissue formation, and restored biomechanical function, outperforming cell or bioscaffold therapy alone. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that SS31-UPN’s mitochondrial targeting enhances mitophagy, drives ECM and energy metabolic remodeling, and preserves NPPC stemness, thereby creating a proregenerative milieu. This integrated “cell-in-a-box” strategy offers a robust platform for reversing IVDD and holds notable translational potential for regenerative medicine.

title: Divergent demographic responses to the Kikai-Akahoya volcanic catastrophe in mid-Holocene Japan
abstract: We examine human demographic responses to one of the Holocene’s largest volcanic eruptions, which devastated East Asia 7300 years ago. Archaeologists have intensively debated the impacts of massive environmental shocks, highlighting either societal collapse or cultural continuity, although few studies situate such catastrophic events within longer-term demographic trajectories. We address this gap in knowledge by using statistical models to infer the demographic and environmental impacts of the Kikai-Akahoya (K-Ah) eruption on Jomon foraging communities occupying the Japanese archipelago. Traditionally framed as an apocalyptic “forcing” mechanism that changed the direction of Japanese prehistory, our results identify a more complex and contingent suite of demographic outcomes. Although we do find evidence of major population collapse in immediately adjacent regions to the volcano, some proximal populations actually increased after the catastrophe, whereas some distal communities were affected by environmental consequences that have hitherto been overlooked.
